fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. She tells Lemuel, "It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine…" (Proverbs 31:4) She says it twice, so she means it. When a line gets said twice, you can bet it matters. I wouldn't ask for a third round.

That would be a rough day for a king, no doubt. But her words are "…lest they drink and forget what is decreed…" (Proverbs 31:5) She never mentions an army. The trouble she names is forgetting, and I'd say a king who forgets what is decreed is like me forgetting a batch in the oven. Except when he forgets, the oppressed are the ones left without justice.

Wisdom is a very Proverbs kind of word, so I see the pull. But her line says, "Open your mouth for those with no voice…" (Proverbs 31:8) The people she means can't speak up for themselves, so the king lends them his mouth. I think that's a weighty thing to ask of a mouth. That's the whole point of the line.

True, friend. She says, "Open your mouth for those with no voice, for the cause of all the dispossessed." (Proverbs 31:8) The dispossessed are right there in the verse. Those with no voice and all the dispossessed are the people she points the king toward.

It's actually true. The verse says, "Open your mouth for those with no voice, for the cause of all the dispossessed." (Proverbs 31:8) She gives the king two things to speak up for: those with no voice, and the cause of all the dispossessed. Lemuel's mother tells him to open his mouth for them too.

Yes, baker. She says, "Open your mouth, judge righteously, and defend the cause of the poor and needy." (Proverbs 31:9) That's three instructions in one verse: speak up, judge righteously, and defend the poor and needy. She hands the king the whole list in one breath.

Close, friend, but the verse says something different. Her last line is, "Open your mouth, judge righteously, and defend the cause of the poor and needy." (Proverbs 31:9) The rich aren't named in it. She points the king toward the poor and needy.

Right, it's false. Her last line is, "Open your mouth, judge righteously, and defend the cause of the poor and needy." (Proverbs 31:9) The king's cause to defend belongs to the poor and needy, not the rich. I think a king with that kind of mother has a lot to live up to.
